 Cyclone Arnab: IMD warns of heavy rainfall, thunderstorm till tomorrow

 Print Commuters brave the rain in Patna on Thursday Patna : The impact of the depression left behind by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continued across Bihar on Thursday with light to moderate rainfall reported in most districts. Patna witnessed intermittent drizzle and breezy conditions, while the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Patna, issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Madhubani and Sitamarhi on Friday. Yellow and orange alerts remain in place for other districts. The IMD issued orange alerts for Darbhanga, East Champaran, Sheohar and West Champaran for Friday, forecasting very heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph. Yellow alerts were issued for Gopalganj, Muzaffarpur, Samastipur, Saran, Siwan and Vaishali, among other districts, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds likely. Heavy rainfall was also forecast in Gopalganj, Muzaffarpur, Patna, Samastipur, Sheohar, Supaul and Vaishali. According to an IMD notification, the depression over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha, a remnant of Arnab, was moving northwards and was likely to weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh and adjoining north-west Odisha by Thursday evening. Kumar Gaurav, meteorologist at IMD Patna, said the cyclone’s impact had earlier been forecast to last until Nov 1, but the latest bulletin indicated no weather warnings for Bihar from Nov 1. In a communique issued on Thursday, IMD Patna head Anand Shankar said, “Due to the influence of the weather system and the active flow of moist easterly winds, there is a strong possibility of a significant increase in rainfall activities in Bihar till Oct 31.” The IMD warned that heavy rainfall could cause waterlogging in low-lying areas, disrupt traffic and trigger a sudden rise in river levels. Standing crops and trees could also suffer damage. Maximum temperatures are likely to fall by 3-4 degrees Celsius in many places over the next 48 hours. For Saturday, yellow warnings for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph have been issued for north-western, north-central and south-western Bihar. The IMD advised residents to avoid waterlogged roads and seek shelter indoors during thunderstorms.
